name: March 19, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 19, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Guldimann call6d the meeting to order at 6:38 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance Via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Cayley Jenner, Vice Chair Suzanne Guldimann; and Commissioners
  Georgia Goldfarb (arrived at 6:45 p.m.), Alicia Peak, and Dane Skophammer

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Alexis Brown, Deputy
  City Manager; Kate Manisco, Recreation Manager; Sebastian Spiroglou, Recreation
  Coordinator; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Jenner led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Goldfarb was absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on March 14, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Introduction of Recreation Coordinator Sebastian Spiroglou

  Recreation Manager Manisco introduced Recreation Coordinator Sebastian
  Spiroglou. She stated Mr. Spiroglou would be responsible for Malibu Bluffs Park,
  Community Programs, and Adult Sports.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Robert Brinkmann stated the Malibu Marlins Swim Team had dedicated pool lanes
  at the Malibu Community Pool as of March 1 1. He expressed frustration regarding
  it taking eight months to get pool time for the organization.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 6:45 p.m.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the October 17, 2023
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting and the January l6,
  2024 Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthlv Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services
  Department in January and February 2024.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  Swim Team Program
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the recommendation ofthe Independent Contract
  Review Ad Hoc Committee regarding the Swim Team Program; and 2) Provide
  feedback to staff.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Manisco stated that
  any swim groups, including those from neighboring cities, could respond to the
  Request for Qualifications. She stated the Malibu Aquatics Foundation, and the
  Malibu Marlins were two Malibu-based organizations that had expressed interest
  in the contract for the swim team. She stated staff would work with a panel of
  aquatics professionals to review the proposals.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Malibu
  Marlins and Malibu Aquatics Foundation were using the pool simultaneously on
  most days. She stated staff had not witnessed challenges between the groups.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 19, 2024
  Page 3 of 7

Robert Brinkmann stated the Malibu Marlins had no issue sharing pool space with
the Malibu Aquatics Foundation.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Mr. Brinkmann stated pool space could
be an issue if a swim team had higher participation, requiring additional lanes.

Commissioner Peak stated the ad hoc committee met with the Malibu Marlins and
Malibu Aquatics Foundation; however, the Malibu Marlins did not provide a lot of
information during a recent meeting. She stated the Malibu Aquatics Foundation
planned to provide the Malibu Marlins with a program proposal outlining how the
two groups could share pool space. She recommended staff proceed with preparing
and releasing the Request for Qualifications.

Vice Chair Guldimann stated there had been many acrimonious comments and
anger on both sides. She inquired if both groups could agree to share pool space.

Commissioner Skophammer stated the two groups could coexist as separate teams.
He stated a merger was not likely, and recommended the Commission approve
moving forward with preparing the Request for Qualifications.

Vice Chair Guldimann thanked Commissioners Peak and Skophammer for their
involvement, hard work, and dedication over the last several months.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Master
Facility Use Agreement between the City and school district does not allow the City
to sublease pool lanes. She stated organizations would rent the pool from the Santa
Monica-Malibu Unified School District.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated
the City would award the swim contract to one vendor. She stated two swim teams
could use the pool during the spring session due to the cancellation of the water
polo program.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated staff had an obligation to fill the unused swim lanes due to the cancellation
of the water polo program. She stated the unique circumstance, allowed the Malibu
Marlins swim time to fill the unused space.

Commissioner Peak stated the Malibu Marlins and Malibu Aquatics Foundation
offered the same swim program, and the contract should be awarded to one
organization.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated the Department does not award
contracts for the same program.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 19, 2024
  Page 4 of 7

  Recreation Manager Manisco stated the City manages the pool for approximately
  25 hours a week. She stated staff had provided the Malibu Marlins the option to
  offer two programs due to availability. She stated additional pool space would not
  be available if the Malibu Marlins offered all their requested programs.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the swim team has historically used all
  the pool lanes and staff had scheduled fewer lanes for lap swimmers.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the pool
  was scheduled at maximum capacity. She stated the City would normally accept
  swim team registrations after the registration deadline but did not allow it during
  the current session due to capacity limits.

  Commissioner Goldfarb disagreed with Commissioners Peak and Skophammer.
  She stated the Commission should not release a Request for Qualifications because
  they were uncomfortable choosing one organization. She believed the Malibu
  Marlins and Malibu Aquatics Foundation could share the pool space and have two
  separate agreements. She stated if water polo returned during the fall season, pool
  space would be limited for both swim team organizations.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated the Department should have a structure to award
  contracts especially due to limited availability. She stated it would also set a
  precedence for field use.

  Chair Jenner stated releasing a Request for Qualifications would be the best option.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Vice Chair Guldimann stated staff could
  start the process and release the Request for Qualifications which required the
  Commission to make a decision.

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Vice Chair Guldimann seconded a motion
  that the Commission recommended staff prepare and release a Request for
  Qualifications for the Aquatics Program and award the contract for services to
  begin Fall 2024.

  Commissioner Goldfarb suggested meeting with the swim team organizations to
  determine if they could agree on a schedule for both teams to utilize the pool.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated the Commission should release the Request for
  Qualifications.

  In response to Recreation Manager Manisco. Commissioner Skophammer stated
  that a second contract could be offered if minimum enrollment numbers were
  unmet.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua clarified the motion.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-1, Commissioner Goldfarb
  dissenting.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Citv-Owned Vacant Land Outreach Plan
  Recommended Action: l) Receive a presentation on City-owned vacant lots; and
  2) Provide input to staff and consultant on an outreach plan.

  Community Services Director Riesgo introduced Deputy City Manager Brown.

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff report and introduced Alyson
  Nichols from Tripepi Smith & Associates.

  Ms. Nichols asked Commissioners which outreach tactics worked best to gamer the
  most part1c1pation.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated community  workshops,  newspaper
  advertisements, and broad focus groups worked best.

  Commissioner Peak stated focus groups with stakeholders would help gather the
  differences in needs.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated that residents needed information about each
  property's limitations and realistic opportunities with each vacant property.

  Commissioner Peak stated staff and consultants should complete an analysis to
  determine what could be done on the properties before meeting with the
  community.

  Commissioner Goldfarb indicated agreement with Vice Chair Guldimann and
  Commissioner Peak. She suggested compiling videos of each property. She stated
  newspapers and press releases were influential.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Deputy City Manager Brown stated the goal of
  the outreach would determine the community’s priorities. She stated buying back
  property related to the transportation funds would be at the discretion of City
  Council.

  Commissioner Peak stated the City should use the data from the 201 2 Parks Master
  Plan report.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 19, 2024
  Page 6 of 7

  Deputy City Manager Brown stated the outreach data would be compiled into a
  report for each property. She stated accurate and current information was essential
  to the proj ect rather than relying on a report that was completed over 10 years ago.
  Commissioner Peak suggested contacting the Parent Teacher Association (PTA) at
  each school. She stated a survey would be important.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the goal was to determine what the community
  wanted and the proper location.

  In response to Ms. Nichols, Commissioner Goldfarb stated hybrid meetings would
  have higher attendance.

  Commissioner Peak suggested recording the meetings.

  In response to Ms. Nichols, Commissioner Skophammer stated the outreach
  process should not last more than three months.

  Commissioner Peak stated the outreach process should be done in six months.

  In response to Ms. Nichols, Vice Chair Guldimann stated weekend meetings should
  be held at various times. She stated meetings could take place at the schools, Malibu
  City Hall, and Point Dume Clubhouse.

  Chair Jenner suggested incorporating a Quick Response (QR) code on all outreach
  information.

  Vice Chair Guldimann suggested incorporating visuals of each property and
  allowing the community to tour the properties.

  Deputy City Manager Brown stated a report on the outreach outcomes would be
  presented to City Council, leading to a City Master Plan.

  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award
  Recommended Action: Discuss the nomination process for the 2024 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion
  to continue Items 5.B. and 5.C. to the April l6, 2024 Regular meeting. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Permanent Skate Park Fundraising
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding fundraising
  efforts for the Permanent Skate Park.

  This item was continued to the April 16, 2024 Regular meeting.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  None.
ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak stated the City did not have a softball field and suggested
  turning a portion of the multipurpose field at Malibu Bluffs Park into a girls‘
  softball field.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 9:05 p.m., Vice Chair Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a
  motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu on April 16‘ 2024.

  SUMNE GULorMANN, Vice Chair
